title: Strict bounded flat tensor presentations and qcqs direct-image continuity
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and separated finite-type $k$-schemes $X,Y$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a qcqs $k$-morphism, and let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring with $R_Z=p_Z^*R$ on the small pro-étale sites [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, def-weil-size-convention]. Use ordinary unbounded module-object derived categories and their ring-sheaf identification [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison]. Put $L=Lf_R^*=f_R^*$ and $G=Rf_{R*}$. Let $I$ be a small nonempty filtered category and $(P_i)$ a diagram of flat $R_Y$-modules with a colimit cocone $v_i:P_i\to C$ in $R_Y$-modules [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Assume $C$, all $f_R^*P_i$, and $f_R^*C$ are flat, meaning tensoring with each is exact [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Let $K\in D(R_X)$ and choose a representing complex $K^\bullet$ zero below an integer $a$. For complexes use direct-sum total tensor and let $Q$ denote passage to the derived category [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves, def-weil-abstract-derived-category].
Then $f_R^*C$ with legs $f_R^*v_i$ is the module colimit of $(f_R^*P_i)$. The strict diagram $E_i^\bullet=K^\bullet\otimes_{R_X}f_R^*P_i$ and $E^\bullet=K^\bullet\otimes_{R_X}f_R^*C$ vanish below $a$, represent $K\otimes^L LP_i$ and $K\otimes^L LC$, and the tensor cocone identifies $\varinjlim_iE_i^\bullet=E^\bullet$ termwise. There exists a K-flat representative $A^\bullet$ of $GK$ with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution]; for any such representative, the canonical map $\varinjlim_i(A^\bullet\otimes P_i)\to A^\bullet\otimes C$ is an isomorphism of complexes, representing the corresponding derived tensors and their actual tensor legs.
There exists a functorial K-injective replacement $J$, equipped with a natural quasi-isomorphism from the identity functor on complexes [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]; for any such replacement, the map induced by the strict tensor cocone gives a canonical isomorphism in $D(R_Y)$
$$Q\bigl(\varinjlim_i f_{R*}J(E_i^\bullet)\bigr)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(f_{R*}J(E^\bullet))\cong G(K\otimes^L LC).$$
Here every colimit inside $Q$ is degreewise in sheaves of modules; its legs are $G(1_K\otimes Lv_i)$. The assertion is independent of the functorial quasi-isomorphic replacements, and asserts no colimit universal property in the ordinary triangulated derived category. K-injective replacement means a functorial quasi-isomorphism to complexes whose Hom complex out of every acyclic complex is acyclic [def-pur-kinjective-complex, prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist].

proof.text: Work in sheaves of modules on the small site representatives. The cited exact monoidal equivalence identifies their flat objects, total tensors, K-flat complexes, and derived pullback and pushforward with the module-object constructions in the statement. It also preserves the specified adjunction, so the ordinary pullback is left adjoint to ordinary pushforward. Its colimits are transported colimits: applying the equivalence and its inverse to the factorization defining a colimit gives the same unique factorization. The site representatives and the diagram are small relative to the module universe, as required by the resolution and tensor-colimit statements below.

source.place: Lemma 5.3(1), proof of (5.4), p. 14; strict tensor specialization for rational proper base change paragraph (1)

proof.text:
Pull back the given cocone. For any $R_X$-module $N$, the adjunction gives
$\operatorname{Hom}(f_R^*C,N)=\operatorname{Hom}(C,f_{R*}N)=\lim_i\operatorname{Hom}(P_i,f_{R*}N)=\lim_i\operatorname{Hom}(f_R^*P_i,N)$.
These bijections send restriction along $f_R^*v_i$ to restriction along $v_i$. Thus they prove the colimit universal property with exactly the asserted legs. This is the elementary colimit argument for a left adjoint, not an assertion that a derived-category colimit exists.

source.place: Lemma 5.3(1), proof of (5.4), p. 14; strict tensor specialization for rational proper base change paragraph (1)

proof.text: For a flat sheaf T, flat-single normalization makes T[0] K-flat and identifies total tensor with T[0] with the complex whose terms are K^r tensor T. Consequently all terms below a vanish. Use the published natural comparison qTensor, which is invertible when either complex is K-flat: at each pulled-back coefficient and at the apex, the second factor is K-flat. Invert these components and compose with the specified isomorphism Q(Kc) ≅ K. Naturality of qTensor gives every transition and cocone-leg square, simultaneously in the coefficient variable. The exact pullback functor commutes with single complexes and localization, so its mapDerivedCategoryFactors isomorphism identifies these tensors with derivedPulledTensor, naturally in the coefficients.

source.place: Lemma 5.3(1), proof of (5.4), p. 14; strict tensor specialization for rational proper base change paragraph (1)

proof.text: For each $r$, apply preservation of module-sheaf colimits by $K^r\otimes_{R_X}-$ to the pulled-back cocone of step 2. Its comparison has legs $1_{K^r}\otimes f_R^*v_i$. Tensor functoriality makes the comparisons commute with $d_K^r\otimes1$; their inverses do so as well. Hence these degreewise comparisons assemble to an isomorphism of complexes $\operatorname{colim}_iE_i^\bullet\cong E^\bullet$ with precisely the tensor cocone, not just an objectwise isomorphism. Here tensoring with a degree-zero complex has only one potentially nonzero summand in every total degree.

source.place: Lemma 5.3(1), proof of (5.4), p. 14; strict tensor specialization for rational proper base change paragraph (1)

proof.text: Choose a complex representing GK and apply the existing flat-term K-flat resolution theorem. For every K-flat representative A of GK, tensorWith A preserves coefficient-sized colimits by the same tensor totalization argument as in step 4. The published qTensor comparison is invertible because its first factor A is K-flat. Its naturality, followed by the specified Q(A) ≅ GK, identifies the whole strict tensor diagram and its actual cocone legs with the derived tensors. No boundedness of A or GK is needed.

source.place: Lemma 5.3(1), proof of (5.4), p. 14; strict tensor specialization for rational proper base change paragraph (1)

proof.text: The small-site K-injective theorem supplies a functorial augmentation eta: id → J. For any such J, the right-derived-functor unit is invertible on J(M). Composing this unit with the inverse of Q(eta_M) gives a natural isomorphism from Q(f_* J(M)) to G(Q(M)), exactly the replacementComparison in the statement. Its naturality is proved from the naturality of eta and the right-derived unit, keeping the quotient-to-localization comparison explicit. Combining with step 3 identifies all actual strict tensor legs after G.

source.place: Lemma 5.3(1), proof of (5.4), p. 14; strict tensor specialization for rational proper base change paragraph (1)

proof.text: First use the ring-sheaf direct image with coefficients f_*R_X. The K-injective comparison with its specified right derived functor identifies the homology of each strict replacement with the higher direct image of the original complex. Bounded direct-image continuity applied to the uniformly bounded original diagram makes this homology cocone a colimit. Exact filtered colimits of module sheaves imply that the canonical strict replacement colimit map is a quasi-isomorphism: compare its homology with the unique isomorphism between the two colimit cocones, and check the comparison on every leg. This works for an arbitrary colimit cocone by transport from the chosen one. Finally factor f_R* as ring-sheaf direct image followed by restriction of scalars along R_Y → f_*R_X. Restriction of scalars is exact and preserves coefficient-sized colimits, as detected through the faithful exact functors to abelian sheaves. It therefore preserves this quasi-isomorphism and transports its strict colimit map to the specified replacedPush map. Localization makes it invertible. The colimit desc equation and step 6 naturality give the normalized equation on every actual leg.

source.place: Lemma 5.3(1), proof of (5.4), p. 14; strict tensor specialization for rational proper base change paragraph (1)

proof.text:
For replacement independence, let $J'$ with $\eta'$ be another functorial K-injective replacement. The natural zigzag
$J(E)\xrightarrow{\eta'_{J(E)}}J'J(E)\xleftarrow{J'(\eta_E)}J'(E)$
consists of quasi-isomorphisms between K-injectives, for each complex $E$. Indeed $J'$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms by naturality of $\eta'$ and two-out-of-three. By the K-injective Hom theorem these arrows are homotopy equivalences; applying the additive $f_{R*}$ preserves the homotopies. At $E_i$ and at $E^\bullet$ this is a natural zigzag of cocones. Exact filtered colimits preserve the resulting objectwise quasi-isomorphisms, by the exact-colimit homology theorem. After $Q$, it identifies the sources, targets, comparison maps and every leg for the two choices. The target identifications are the normalized K-injective computations of step 6, so these identifications also respect $G(1_K\otimes Lv_i)$. Compatibility with the normalized target follows from naturality of the right-derived-functor unit on maps between K-injectives and the augmentation equations; equality of the strict cocone squares is checked on colimit coprojections.

Step 3: the flat-single normalization holds for unbounded C, and naturality in the coefficient comes from a K-flat resolution B->K (B tensor T -> K tensor T is a quasi-iso because T tensor - is exact). Step 8: the zigzag of quasi-isos between K-injectives gives homotopy equivalences, which f_* preserves. Edge cases checked: one-object I with f = id, zero K or ring, constant diagram, J(K) unbounded below. No duplicate of the item found. The generic off-unit tool_uses are accepted.
